utterances.text: So you, you've described, you later received some, well, if you like, assurance or permission to adapt the second stage in a way that made you less gloomy and pessimistic yourself about where it would all lead.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And when -- can you remember: When do you say that you were directed to implement the second stage?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will talk about the second stage, and I will touch upon several points. In January, we already spoke with Goran Zekic about the implementation of the second stage. We also discussed, and I remember such a meeting about rounding off the concept of the Birac region. A definite, final position to implement this was reached in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask for a clarification, Mr. Deronjic? You spoke a few times about your wish to resign and that you finally withdrew your resignation. Could you tell us exactly in time - I might have missed it - exactly in time when this was, when you first discussed the whole of the document or the instructions, or at the beginning of the second stage? When exactly did you offer to resign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at the beginning of the discussion on the implementation of the second stage, we actually held a meeting in Kravica. That is the Serbian region in Bratunac. I have those minutes. If we need to, we can find it, so that I don't misstate what's in it. This is January, or possibly February. And then we seriously discussed the Variant A and B second stage. That was the meeting when I submitted my resignation, and not on the one immediately following the 19th of December, when a meeting was held in Bratunac and when the Crisis Staff was formed, when we issued the instructions for a Serb Assembly to be formed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can see the clock very easily from the way I face the witness. I wonder, may I ask now just one more question, may I, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not after I -- and is one of the parties intending to tender into evidence this -- these minutes of the meeting where Mr. Deronjic offered his resignation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we'll have to check that overnight. I thought they might -- I had understood they were in one of the exhibits, a big chunk of material that was tendered by the Prosecution. But if not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've missed it, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will check it overnight as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that we know that if it's not in, the Chamber could consider to have this evidence to be called by itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: May I ask a single question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's simply: If you could go up, please, in the same document, to first stage, Variant B, first stage, item 6, please, Mr. Deronjic. It refers to setting up secret storage places and depots in local communities. Do you see -- it won't take you long, I think, Mr. Deronjic, to see that paragraph. My question is simply whether -- whether that did happen in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just discussed this at the municipal board meeting. We concluded that we should try to gather financial funds so that we could purchase some of these things. But I don't know whether we actually implemented any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure whether I've stolen about nine seconds or more, but that's -- I have no more questions this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Deronjic, we'll continue to hear your evidence tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom. I see, Madam Registrar, you are not contradicting. So in this same courtroom. May I again instruct you not to speak with anyone, whoever it is, about the evidence you gave in this courtroom and the evidence that you may expect still to be given in this courtroom. Yes, please. Mr. Deronjic may be escorted out of the courtroom. If there's nothing else to be raised at this moment, we'll adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of February 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.
